answer: Split each identity key into five shares held by five peers. First, onboarding splits the key and gives one share to each peer. Second, each epoch the agent needs three shares to sign, and peers refuse copied work histories. Third, shares rotate to new peers each epoch, so a stolen set goes stale fast. Fourth, a peer caught signing for two identities with the same history loses a $500 stake. Faking 1,000 agents means bribing 3,000 peers at $200 each, $600,000. A pearl only leaves its shell when three trusted hands turn the key at dawn, and a haven built that way has no room for ghosts.
